messages:
Mike: CI red on canary build — image push failing on the final manifest upload, getting a 401 from registry. Job: https://ci.internal.redwood.com/jobs/98765

Mike: Log snippet:
```
> time="2025-11-12T14:02:11Z" level=error msg="push failed: unauthorized: authentication required"
> POST /v2/redwood/canary/manifests: 401 Unauthorized
> digest: sha256:...
```

Sara: ugh, same pipeline succeeded for a rerun an hour ago? flaky auth sounds like token rotation or worker creds. Which runner was this on (ephemeral vs dedicated)?

Mike: ephemeral-runner-12, started by canary pipeline. Commit is 0a9b3f5 — we recently changed the Dockerfile to add a root-owned layer for a build artifact (chown in a later stage). CI job uses buildx + remote cache.

Dan: can you try a rerun with --no-cache or forcing a fresh pull? to rule out cached manifest mismatch. Also pinging @Priya from infra to check registry token rotations.

Mike: kicked a rerun with no-cache: https://ci.internal.redwood.com/jobs/98768 (ran at 14:07). CI-Bot: rerun scheduled.

CI-Bot: Job 98768 started on ephemeral-runner-18.

Priya: looking, registry logs show an auth rejection for the same runner ID around that time; token inspector shows a short-lived service token was used and expired mid-request. We rotated a set of tokens earlier today but there should be a grace window.

Sara: hmm could be race where ephemeral worker fetched a token, then the rotation invalidated it before the manifest push. That would explain intermittent passes. Any chance buildx is keeping connections open long enough that token expiry hits the later push phase? :thinking_face:

Dan: also possible: the manifest push uses a separate endpoint and a different HTTP client library that doesn't refresh credentials mid-flight. If rotation happened between layer uploads and manifest push it errors.

Mike: the no-cache rerun failed with the same 401, so not cache. Stack trace shows manifest POST occurs ~30s after the last blob upload.

Priya: workaround for the canary: I'm going to temporarily extend rotation window by 5 minutes and push a one-off token fix for ephemeral runners. Will report back in 10.

Dan: long-term: either make the registry token refreshable by the runner, or have the build driver re-auth before manifest push. Recommend a small change to the buildx wrapper to re-fetch creds right before final push. I can open a PR.

Mike: sounds good. For immediate unblock, can someone rerun the canary pipeline after Priya's change? I don't want to keep spamming infra if it needs a window.

Priya: I've extended the rotation window. Please rerun.

Mike: rerun triggered: https://ci.internal.redwood.com/jobs/98772

CI-Bot: Job 98772 completed — SUCCESS. :tada:

Mike: good, canary passed. I'll leave a follow-up ticket to add the pre-push credential refresh and add a small test that simulates token expiry during a multi-step push.

Sara: <@Dan> can you own the PR to fetch creds before push? Label it eng-infra / high priority for the short-lived token triage.

Dan: yep, will open PR and add a unit test that fakes expiry.

Mike: filing ticket and adding notes about the ephemeral runner token lifecycle. Thanks everyone. :thumbsup:
